Two-group trial scenario

Source: R/ms_scenario.R
ms_scenario.Rd

Combines the models of the control and treatment groups, the allocation ratio and the accrual.

Usage

ms_scenario(
  control,
  treatment,
  allocation = 1,
  accrual,
  pfs_switch = c("event", "censor"),
  switch_start = 0
)

Arguments

control, treatment

ms_model objects of the control and treatment groups.

allocation

Allocation ratio, treatment to control (for example 2 for 2:1).

accrual

An ms_accrual object.

pfs_switch

Definition of PFS at a switch before progression: "event" (followed up to progression or death) or "censor" (censored at the switch). It applies to both groups.

switch_start

Calendar time (time since the start of accrual) from which switching after progression is possible, nonnegative. The default 0 means that switching is possible from randomization, as in the models.

Value

An object of class ms_scenario, a list with the two models, allocation, the allocation probabilities prob (control, treatment), accrual, pfs_switch and switch_start. The models carry pfs_switch as well.

Details

pfs_switch defines PFS for patients who switch before progression (switch_pre in ms_model). With "event", the switch does not change the definition: PFS is the time to progression or death. With "censor", PFS is censored at the switch (for example when the start of a new treatment censors PFS); the log-rank test of PFS then compares the hazard prog + death of the patients who are progression-free and have not switched.

switch_start is a calendar time (time since the start of accrual) before which nobody switches, for example when switching is allowed only after an interim analysis. A patient enrolled at time e can then switch from the follow-up time max(switch_start - e, 0) on: progressions before that time do not lead to a switch at progression, and patients who progressed before it can switch with switch_rate from that time on. The distribution of OS then depends on the entry time, and the computations for OS integrate over the entry time. They cover the OS log-rank statistic alone with mean = "direct"; two endpoints together, an OS test at looks driven by PFS events, and a PFS test at looks driven by OS events with a variance other than "null" give an error. PFS is not affected by the switching. Under the null hypothesis the score no longer has independent increments when the switching changes the death hazard: the correlations between the looks are computed from the per-patient influence functions instead of the information (see lr_cov). switch_start cannot be combined with switching before progression (switch_pre).

See also

ms_model, ms_accrual, ms_null

Examples

ctl <- ms_model(death = log(2) / 12)
trt <- ms_model(death = 0.7 * log(2) / 12)
ms_scenario(ctl, trt, accrual = ms_accrual(rate = 20))
#> Two-group scenario, allocation 1:1 (treatment:control)
#> 
#> Control group. Four-state model for one group (clock after progression: "reset")
#> Before progression (time since randomization):
#>  time prog      death switch_prob dropout
#>     0    0 0.05776227           0       0
#> 
#> Treatment group. Four-state model for one group (clock after progression: "reset")
#> Before progression (time since randomization):
#>  time prog      death switch_prob dropout
#>     0    0 0.04043359           0       0
#> 
#> Piecewise uniform accrual by rates (patients per unit time):
#>  time rate
#>     0   20

# Switching after progression in the control group, possible only from
# month 15 (for example after an interim analysis)
ctl_sw <- ms_model(prog = 0.1, death = 0.01, death_prog = 0.05,
                   switch_prob = 0.3, switch_rate = 0.04, death_switch = 0.03)
trt_sw <- ms_model(prog = 0.06, death = 0.008, death_prog = 0.045)
ms_scenario(ctl_sw, trt_sw, accrual = ms_accrual(rate = 20), switch_start = 15)
#> Two-group scenario, allocation 1:1 (treatment:control)
#> 
#> Control group. Four-state model for one group (clock after progression: "reset")
#> Before progression (time since randomization):
#>  time prog death switch_prob dropout
#>     0  0.1  0.01         0.3       0
#> After progression (time since progression):
#>  time_post death_prog switch_rate death_switch
#>          0       0.05        0.04         0.03
#> 
#> Treatment group. Four-state model for one group (clock after progression: "reset")
#> Before progression (time since randomization):
#>  time prog death switch_prob dropout
#>     0 0.06 0.008           0       0
#> After progression (time since progression):
#>  time_post death_prog switch_rate death_switch
#>          0      0.045           0        0.045
#> 
#> Switching possible from calendar time 15 (time since the start of accrual)
#> 
#> Piecewise uniform accrual by rates (patients per unit time):
#>  time rate
#>     0   20
